content: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose and other organic compounds. The overall reaction can be summarized as: 6COâ + 6HâO + light energy â CâHââOâ + 6Oâ. This process occurs in two main stages: the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions). In the light-dependent reactions, which take place in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts, chlorophyll and other pigments capture photons, exciting electrons that flow through electron transport chains. This electron flow powers the creation of ATP (through chemiosmosis) and NADPH, while also splitting water molecules to release oxygen. The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma of chloroplasts, using the ATP and NADPH from light-dependent reactions to fix carbon dioxide into organic compounds. The enzyme RuBisCO catalyzes the addition of COâ to RuBP (ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate), eventually producing glucose after multiple cycle iterations. Photosynthetic efficiency depends on environmental factors including light intensity, COâ concentration, temperature, and water availability. Limiting any essential factor reduces the overall rateâthis is known as Liebig's Law of the Minimum. Too much light can damage photosystems, while insufficient COâ (under 200 ppm) severely restricts carbon fixation. Water stress causes stomata to close, reducing COâ intake while protecting against dehydration.

scenario.title: Terrarium Ecosystem Lab
scenario.content: Students design and maintain virtual terrariums, balancing environmental factors to optimize plant growth. The simulation visualizes photosynthetic processes at the cellular and molecular levels, showing light absorption, electron transport, and carbon fixation in real-time. Students can adjust light intensity, spectrum, duration, COâ concentration, water availability, and temperature, observing how these changes affect photosynthetic rate and plant development. The system provides data on oxygen production, glucose synthesis, and growth metrics while displaying visual indicators of plant health. Interactive tools allow students to examine leaf cellular structure, track carbon atoms through the Calvin cycle, and measure energy conversion efficiency under different conditions. Challenge scenarios require students to design self-sustaining ecosystems or optimize growth under resource constraints, teaching ecological balance and photosynthetic adaptation.

hypothesis.description: Students will trace energy and matter transformations in photosynthesis by analyzing how environmental inputs become biological outputs. They will predict how changes in light, water, and carbon dioxide availability affect photosynthetic efficiency, and explain the interconnections between photosynthetic processes and ecosystem function.
